title: SCALE: Constructing Structured Natural Language Comment Trees for Software Vulnerability Detection

key_numbers.value: 62.85% (SCALE) vs 56.04% best baseline (UniXcoder; CodeBERT 49.10% is the worst, not best, baseline)

key_numbers.metric: CodeBERT F1 gain from SCT-enhanced representation

structure_gain: SCALE (AST + LLM-generated comment tree) improves F1 by 1.17-13.47 points over best pre-trained/LLM baseline across three datasets (Table 3); RQ4 ablation shows removing SCT-Enhanced Representation module degrades performance.
stop_detail: ChatGPT-generated per-statement comments are inserted as sibling/parent nodes into a Tree-sitter AST via row-position matching, then 11 syntax-category rules replace AST node values with comment text to build the structured comment tree (Section 3.1-3.2).

title: ContractTinker: LLM-Empowered Vulnerability Repair for Real-World Smart Contracts
structure_gain: none reported (no raw-code-only baseline or no-CDG condition tested)
stop_detail: Slither-derived Contextual Dependency Graph prunes to vulnerability-relevant elements before Chain-of-Thought prompting; multi-agent debate with an independent LLM validator plus a compilation check gates accepted patches (§2.2-§2.4, §4.2.2)

title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Vulnerability Detection Under Variable Context Windows

key_numbers.metric: models robust to context-length (both null hypotheses accepted)
key_numbers.value: GPT-4; Mistral-7B and Mixtral-8x7B at 32,768-token context window

title: VulBinLLM: LLM-powered Vulnerability Detection for Stripped Binaries
structure_gain: Decompilation optimization (vulnerability-annotated, simplified, renamed pseudocode) plus memory-management agent yields ~10% average accuracy gain and up to ~37-point F1 gain (CWE-190) over LATTE baseline on Juliet binaries (Table 3); no controlled representation-only ablation is reported.
stop_detail: GPT-4o annotates decompiled Ghidra pseudocode with vulnerability-flagging comments, simplifies control structures, and renames variables; a memory-management agent queues functions and stores/retrieves per-function summarized analysis in a SQL archival store to work around context-window limits (VulBinLLM architecture section, Figure 3).

title: VerilogLAVD: LLM-Aided Rule Generation for Vulnerability Detection in Verilog

key_numbers.metric: Illegal rule-usage rate with validation FSM

structure_gain: VeriPG graph (AST + control/data dependency) plus LLM-generated traversal rules improves F1 over LLM+external-knowledge baseline by 0.32 (GPT-4o: 0.57 vs 0.25) and 0.16 (DeepSeek-V3: 0.50 vs 0.34), same backbone LLMs held fixed (Table 2).
stop_detail: LLM performs chain-of-thought extraction of vulnerability conditions from CWE text into JSON-structured rules (functions/filters/paths), symbolically executed via traversal over the VeriPG property graph, with a validation FSM checking primitive usage during rule generation (rule-generation and Table 3 sections).

title: Learning to Triage Vulnerability Reports from Program Analysis: An Empirical Study in Node.js
structure_gain: The text-only LLM (raw code snippet + nearby data-flow context, 0.915 F1) outperforms the graph-only GNN (0.886 F1) and the concatenated LLM+GNN hybrid (0.902 F1); adding graph structure does not improve over the text representation alone here
stop_detail: No cross-modal grounding; the hybrid model concatenates independently-learned LLM text embeddings and GNN provenance-graph embeddings with end-to-end backprop, no attention/alignment mechanism (§3.4)

title: A Systematic Study of Code Obfuscation Against LLM-based Vulnerability Detection

key_numbers.metric: virtualization-obfuscation attack success rate (downgrade), C/C++ datasets
detection success-rate gap, existence-only vs. type+location scoring criterion
key_numbers.value: ~40% average increase under existence-only vs. type/location criterion

structure_gain: Central ablation compares raw code text vs. its obfuscated (layout/data-flow/control-flow-transformed) counterpart, same LLM/prompt: virtualization obfuscation degrades detection with up to ~80% attack success rate on C/C++ (Finding #2); conversely some layout obfuscations (e.g., L1) 'upgrade' detection by removing misleading surface cues, e.g. QWEN-14B on PrimeVul jumps from 0.39 to 0.80 success after L1 (Section 4.2.3).
stop_detail: No external grounding/retrieval mechanism is used; detection is single-turn prompting of raw (possibly obfuscated) source code, scored on a 1-4 rubric checking existence, type, and location match against ground truth (Section 4.1 Evaluation Metrics).

title: Beyond Function-Level Analysis: Context-Aware Reasoning for Inter-Procedural Vulnerability Detection

key_numbers.metric: PrimeVul accuracy, function-only vs full CPRVul

structure_gain: Reported +11.13pp (56.65%->67.78%) compares UniXcoder (encoder classifier) vs fine-tuned Qwen2.5-32B — different architectures, so the gain is NOT representation-isolated; fine-tuning-budget equality is unsubstantiated.
stop_detail: Model selection uses best checkpoint by validation-set performance; structured reasoning grounds the final label in explicit 'observation / security_reasoning / impact' JSON fields generated before the verdict (Phase II reasoning description)

title: How Code Representation Shapes False-Positive Dynamics in Cross-Language LLM Vulnerability Detection

key_numbers.metric: FPR escalation with text fine-tuning (Qwen3-8B, OWASP Java)
key_numbers.value: 0.763 zero-shot -> 0.866 pilot -> 1.000 full-scale, while F1 stays 0.637-0.688

key_numbers.metric: FPR reduction switching text-trained model's input to AST, no retraining (Qwen3-8B)

key_numbers.value: FPR reduction of Delta=-0.527 under text->AST switch

structure_gain: Switching a text-fine-tuned model's inference-time input from raw text to pruned AST (no retraining) cuts FPR by 0.282-0.527 depending on CWE, with only a modest F1 cost (e.g. 0.688->0.637 for Qwen3-8B), same model weights and training budget -- a pure representation-only manipulation
stop_detail: No grounding/stop mechanism reported; this is an empirical characterization study without a deployable technique or explicit stopping criterion

title: Revisiting Vul-RAG: Reproducibility and Replicability of RAG-based Vulnerability Detection with Open-Weight Models

key_numbers.value: identical pairwise accuracy; balanced recall/precision differ by <=2pp

key_numbers.metric: performance plateau across all evaluated open-weight models

structure_gain: none reported -- the RAG knowledge-base/retrieval representation is held fixed (reused from the original Vul-RAG) across all comparisons; gains/losses are attributed to model family, scale, and reasoning capability, not to representation variation.
stop_detail: Vul-RAG retrieves top-n knowledge-base entries (functional semantics, vulnerability causes, fixing solutions) via BM25 plus re-ranking keyed on LLM-extracted code semantics, then has the LLM sequentially reason over each retrieved item before a final verdict (Section 3, Figure 1).

title: Ethereum NFT Smart Contracts: Knowledge-Guided Vulnerability Detection with LLM and Code Slicing
structure_gain: +13.33pp / +10.0pp deltas correct, but same-model/config constancy is not substantiated (settings 'not recorded') and complete-contract inputs are far longer than slices — unequal context budget.
stop_detail: A structure-aware context-window algorithm regex-locates candidate statements, expands to a syntactically balanced function-scoped slice, and embeds an ERC-721-specific knowledge base plus a closed label set and explicit 'return None if insufficient evidence' rejection rule directly in the prompt (Section 4.2-4.3, Algorithm 1, Prompt 1).
